one_liner: rav1e fork whose default AV1 encode is byte-identical to stock rav1e and about 1.10x faster single-threaded; bundles a rav1d fork.
what_it_does: Two independent Cargo projects in one repo. rusty_av1e is a vendored fork of xiph/rav1e (same library API and `rav1e` CLI, crate renamed to rusty_av1e) with reworked hot kernels in the coefficient-entropy and quantize paths. rusty_av1d is a fork of memorysafety/rav1d, the Rust port of dav1d, and makes no speed claim. A `--racecar off|on|stock` switch picks the byte-identical optimized kernels (default), the kernels plus rav1e's estimated transform-domain rate (output changes), or the original stock code paths for A/B measurement.
how_it_is_fast: Profiling put `write_coeffs_lv_map` (coefficient token coding) at 48.6% and quantize at 12.3% of a speed-6 single-thread encode, and three byte-identical changes were kept. B7a turns the per-scan-position non-zero-map context stencil into a full-area, column-contiguous kernel that can vectorize. B7a-SIMD is a hand-written AVX2 twin of that kernel (one ymm register per column of up to 32 rows, vpminub/vpaddb stencil, vpavgb for (mag+1)>>1). Q2 rewrites quantize's serial main loop branch-free, removing two data-dependent mispredicted branches. Per the ledger the stencil dropped from 878 to 96 ms and the quantize loop from 676-730 to 440-466 ms. `--racecar on` additionally switches on rav1e's existing `tx_domain_rate`/`tx_domain_distortion` options, which replace real token coding in RDO with a table-based rate estimate.
when_to_use: You already ship rav1e and want shorter encodes with output that is byte-identical to the default stock bitstream: 1.058-1.126x single-threaded at speed 6 on the authors' clip, with the full gain on x86-64 CPUs that have AVX2.
Dense, high-rate encodes (low QP), where entropy coding is a larger share of encode time: 1.126x at QP 60 against 1.058x at QP 160.
A pure-Rust, BSD-2 AV1 encoder embedded in a Rust application (it backs AVIF/AV1 encoding in remade_ffmpeg_rs), where a C encoder is not an option.
CPU-bound, bandwidth-insensitive encoding where 50-60% more bytes is acceptable: `--racecar on --tune Psnr` ran about 1.6x faster than the byte-identical mode on the same clip.
when_not_to_use: When encode speed per core is the main goal and a C encoder is acceptable: SVT-AV1 is the catalogued fast AV1 encoder, and a 1.10x gain does not change rav1e's position against it (no cross-encoder numbers here).
Multi-threaded or tiled production encodes: every A/B is `--threads 1 --tiles 1` on one synthetic 640x480 clip, and the gain at default threading is not measured.
aarch64: the AVX2 stencil has no NEON twin yet (ledger item 9), so ARM gets only the portable B7a and Q2 changes, and its speedup is unmeasured.
Bandwidth-limited delivery in `--racecar on`: +60% bitstream and -2.28 dB PSNR at the default tune; a faster stock `--speed` preset may be the better trade, and none was compared.

Long-term dependencies that need upstream fixes: the code is vendored rather than a GitHub fork, upstream tracking is an unchecked roadmap item, there is no CI (PRs #3 and #4 adding a check workflow are still open), and the repo has 0 stars.

integration.form: crate (rusty_av1e 0.8.0 library plus `rav1e` CLI; rusty_av1d 1.2.0 library plus `dav1d` CLI); two separate Cargo projects, no top-level workspace
integration.dependencies: rusty_av1e defaults pull nasm (via nasm-rs and cc) for upstream asm, plus clap/y4m/ivf and the other CLI crates, and maybe-rayon for threading; `default-features = false` gives a no-asm build in which the AVX2 stencil still runs (std runtime detection). rusty_av1d needs nasm for x86 asm.
integration.min_toolchain: rusty_av1e rust-version 1.83.0; rusty_av1d rust-version 1.79 for a stable library build, though its directory pins nightly-2026-02-05
integration.platforms: any rav1e target; x86-64 with AVX2 gets the hand-written stencil (runtime-detected, scalar fallback); upstream x86 and ARM asm kept; Windows, macOS and Linux named in the README
integration.thread_safety: As upstream rav1e (one Context per encode, rayon threads). The fork adds process-global OnceLock latches (racecar mode and about 40 RAV1E_* environment knobs), read once per process and shared by every encoder in it.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same API, same CLI flags and byte-identical default output to stock rav1e 564ae3b0 per the authors, but the crate is renamed (`use rusty_av1e::...`), and the byte-identity is not enforced by any committed test

gotchas: The process environment changes output. About 40 RAV1E_* variables (RAV1E_FAST, RAV1E_TRELLIS, RAV1E_LAMBDA_MULT, RAV1E_MODE_TOPK, RAV1E_WARP_FORCE and others) are latched into statics and alter encoder decisions. RAV1E_RACECAR=0 restores the stock kernels, and RAV1E_HARVEST=<path> appends CSV telemetry and panics if the file cannot be opened.

The 'byte-identical gate' is not automated: tests/profile_encode.rs prints the bitstream FNV and only asserts run-to-run determinism, and the stock hash 688d5eeaee94d95e that the README says is pinned there is not in the file. Byte-identity at HEAD therefore rests on manual checks last ledgered on 2026-07-02, while later tier work landed behind environment gates.

Naming is inverted between layers. On the CLI, `--racecar off` is the optimized default and `on` changes the bitstream, but racecar.rs and the toggle-site comments still describe the pre-remap meaning (racecar on = kernels = default). The dispatch comment says the AVX2 kernel honours RAV1E_CPU_TARGET, but the code calls `is_x86_feature_detected!("avx2")` directly, so RAV1E_CPU_TARGET cannot turn it off.

`--racecar on` uses stock rav1e's own tx-domain rate estimator (off at every stock speed preset), not new fork code. It also forces `tx_domain_distortion` on, working around an upstream assert that the fork's ledger documents: tx_domain_rate with the psychovisual tune panics in `distortion_scale`, reachable through the API or a config file.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: SVT-AV1 is the catalogued fast AV1 encoder (C); pick rusty_av1e only when you are tied to rav1e's Rust API or exact bitstream and want the same output sooner. For decoding, use the catalogued dav1d, or rav1d-safe if you need safe Rust; this repo's rusty_av1d makes no speed claim.
verified_claims_summary: First-party, on an unnamed machine with about 5% thermal noise. The fork's rav1e CLI at 885a2887 against stock rav1e 564ae3b0 (an upstream xiph/rav1e master commit), built with the same unstated flags, encoded one synthetic 640x480, 60-frame ffmpeg testsrc2 clip at --speed 6 --quantizer 100 --tiles 1 --threads 1. Median 6.911 s vs 7.588 s (1.098x over 7 interleaved rounds, every round 1.072-1.117x), with identical 262,180-byte output; a single-binary racecar A/B reproduced 1.079x, and a QP sweep gave 1.058-1.126x. The 1.69x mode changes the bitstream (+60% bytes, -2.28 dB PSNR) and divides by a stock time from a different session; within one session it is 1.61x over the byte-identical mode.
status_note: Last code change 2026-08-02 (113 commits; later commits through 2026-10-04 only edit an install-count banner), BSD-2-Clause plus the AOM patent licence, 0 stars, no issues, no CI. Reasonable to trial as a rav1e drop-in, but a thin, recently forked dependency to build on.
measurement_notes: For the orchestrator: no correctness bug was found behind the 1.098x. The CLI maps `--racecar off` to `racecar::set(true)` (kernels on) and `stock` to `set(false)`, so the default really runs the optimized kernels. All bitstream-changing tier work (trellis, ARNR, warp, top-K, FASTRATE) is gated behind RAV1E_* variables that default to off, with RAV1E_FAST unset meaning off. Measurement caveats beyond the verifier's: (1) the README's 'FNV gate pinned in tests/profile_encode.rs' is not true; the test prints the hash and asserts only determinism. The repo has no CI (PRs #3 and #4 to add a check workflow are open), so byte-identity after 2026-07-02 is unverified, though it is plausible given the environment gating. (2) Every timing is single-thread and single-tile on one synthetic testsrc2 clip; the ledger records only a pre-change all-threads baseline (3.44 Mpx/s) with no after-number. (3) The 1.69x divides a 2026-07-02 nitro-session time (4.586 s) by a stock time from the separate QP-sweep session (7.745 s). Within the nitro session the racecar-kernel arm ran 7.399 s, about 5% slower than the sweep's implied 7.05 s for the same configuration, so cross-session drift is about the size of the claimed default gain. Use 1.61x (same session, against the byte-identical mode) for the opt-in mode. (4) Documentation drift: the README's 'P4' says tx_domain_rate measured about 2x at +49% size while the ledger says 1.62x; harvest.rs describes RAV1E_FAST=fast as about +38% speed at +0.099% BD, while the README reports +5.3%/+3.3%/-8.7% BD-rate per clip for the same tier. The install banner went from 1,002 to 2,768 in a 2026-10-04 docs-only commit. crates.io: rusty_av1e 1,274 downloads, rusty_av1d 1,494. No new leads beyond the already-catalogued Remade-With-Rust repos; the awesome.video directory lists this repo but adds no measurement.
